attacks.unsupported_mechanism: KILLED - claimed 3.2-log inactivation of >=50 um organisms via "UVT-keyed dose control," but UV dose-response for organisms in the 50-200 um size class (e.g., copepod nauplii, veligers) requires fluences orders of magnitude above what 350 m3/h throughput can deliver (well-studied ballast UV systems like Trojan Marinex require either low flow or multi-lamp arrays; 3-log at 50 um is not established at the claimed specific throughput).
attacks.obvious_combination: KILLED - 40 um backwash screen + UV disinfection + dose control keyed to UVT is the standard combination found in commercial marine ballast management systems (e.g., Trojan Marinex, Hyde Marine, Alfa Laval PureBallast, optimized via UVT sensors per AWWA Jtm-UVT guidance); no novel integration is shown.
